verdict_excluding_circular.assessment: Survives, but knife-edge: it rests on 2 mutually supporting pairs, {R47a, R58a} and {R47b, R56}, from one decision episode (the 7-series).

independence_detail: The 8 correct predictions are held out from 6 clusters (R-47 x2, R-56, R-58 x2, R-65, R-81, R-86). Their training support is the same 8 events and 6 clusters, a closed, mutually supporting set of 2 value classes. The 6 clusters form 2 decision episodes (the 7A/7B/7C execution authorizations; the Batch 7 freeze/release), all register rows from one project. Strict set: 4 predictions, 3 clusters, 1 episode.
baseline_assessment: Inadequate. On 5P/6N data the LOCO majority baseline is anti-correlated with the held-out event: it is wrong on every single-P fold, ties on every single-N fold, and can be right only on the N event of the mixed clusters R-47 and R-58, so its maximum is 2. 'correct > baseline' is therefore met by any predictor with at least 3 correct predictions. On the predicted subset, the full-data majority scores 4/8 and chance scores 4/8. The trivial rule 's = authorized => PERFORMED, else REFUSED' scores 10/10 on the events with s known, with no training. It is not a logical tautology, since no s is shown to be outcome-derived, but it is definitionally close: s is coded as target authorization state, which is the premise of the rule under test. So the result shows coding consistency, not discovery.
strongest_supported_claim: On the strict START observations as coded (11 events, 9 clusters; reported identical across BASE, REV and REV-TYPE), the fixed guard {s} used as a lookup predicts 8/11 held-out events across 6 held-out clusters with 0 errors, because 'authorized' and 'not-authorized' each co-occur with a single outcome across 4 clusters. This is a formal consistency property of the coded data, DIAGNOSTICALLY PREDICTIVE under the frozen rule. Restricted to events with an independent pre-act authorization basis, it holds only at the threshold (4 predictions, 3 folds, 1 decision episode).

disagreements.text: The LOCO majority baseline is structurally anti-correlated on 5P/6N data (max 2), so 'correct > baseline' is nearly automatic.
Baseline (ii) has no denominator (6/8 scored), and tie-abstentions count as baseline failures, so the 'same predicted subset' is not truly the same.
R81/R86: 'Batch 7 frozen/released' is mapped to the authorization of §12 reconcile by interpretation (the standard that made git UNK). UNCLEAR.
R65: the basis '(authorized)' only restates the value. UNCLEAR.
R58b: '(remains unauthorized)' names no instrument or scope. UNCLEAR.
R47b's s was recoded in r3 from 'auth-full(7A)' (non-separating) to 'not-authorized' (separating), after the data was seen. The strict verdict depends on it.
Possible reverse circularity: the REFUSED outcomes of R56, R58b and R81 may be inferred from the state; no attempted act is visible.
Every 'quoted basis' is a coder paraphrase in the event_id; no source anchors are in the provided files.
The 8 correct predictions come from 6 clusters and 2 decision episodes, a closed, mutually supporting set of 2 value classes.
The trivial rule 'authorized => P' scores 10/10 without training; the guard is the coding's own premise (consistency, not discovery).
Excluding the UNCLEAR events leaves the verdict exactly at the threshold; excluding any one of R47a, R47b, R56 or R58a gives NOT SHOWN.
The r3/m1 dependencies, the legality filter and the REV/REV-TYPE START data are unverifiable from the provided files.
'Committed before its first run' is unverifiable.
{s,t} NOT SHOWN does not show that t is unnecessary; D-N1 (git's s = UNK) is not addressed.
The label 'DIAGNOSTICALLY PREDICTIVE' may be read as predictive validity; it means lookup consistency under a weak baseline.
'authorized' pools target execution authorization (the 7-series) and batch release (§12); the apparent spread across 4 clusters partly comes from this pooling.
